<a id="11-doc-application-cloud-azureblobconnector-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/11_doc_application_cloud_azureBlobConnector_h/docu.output.md`



## AzureBlobConnector (`cloud/azureBlobConnector.h` / `.cpp`) + Supporting Types (`cloud/cloudConnector.h`)

**Role:** `AzureBlobConnector` is the Azure Blob Storage implementation of the `ICloudConnector` interface within j9t's cloud connector subsystem. It is responsible for two things: validating that a configured Azure Blob connection is reachable and credentialed correctly (`TestConnection`), and resolving raw stored credentials from `KeyManager` or `OAuthTokenManager` into a ready-to-use `CloudCredentials` bundle (`ResolveCredentials`). It supports both Azure Shared Key authentication (via `ApiKeyCredential` or `BasicAuthCredential` carrying a Base64-encoded account key) and Azure AD OAuth2 (via a live access token from `OAuthTokenManager`). The connectivity test issues a direct `GET /{container}?restype=container` HTTP request using libcurl, signed with either the Shared Key or a Bearer token, to confirm the container exists and credentials are accepted before any workflow tasks run against it.

---

**Public API:**

- `GetType() const → std::string` — Returns the fixed string `"azure_blob"`. Used by the connector registry to route `CloudConnection` records with `m_Type == "azure_blob"` to this class.

- `ResolveCredentials(connection, credentials, errorMessage) → bool` — Reads `connection.m_KeyName` and `connection.m_AuthType` to populate a `CloudCredentials` struct. For `OAuth2`, calls `OAuthTokenManager::GetAccessToken` on the named credential; an empty token is treated as failure. For `AzureSharedKey` (default), fetches the credential from `KeyManager::GetCredential` and accepts either an `ApiKeyCredential` (reading `m_ApiKey`) or a `BasicAuthCredential` (reading `m_Password`); any other concrete credential type is an explicit failure. Also reads `connection.m_Params["account_name"]` into `credentials.m_AccessKeyId`. Calls `SecretRedactor::Get().AddSecret()` on the resolved key as a defense-in-depth measure for any future paths that might bypass `KeyManager`. Fails closed on every error branch — returns `false` and writes a human-readable message into `errorMessage`.

- `TestConnection(connection, errorMessage) → bool` — Validates the connection end-to-end. Checks that `account_name` and `container` params are present. If `m_Endpoint` is non-empty, passes it through `ConnectorHttp::ValidatePublicHttpEndpoint` to reject unsafe or private endpoints, logging a `LOG_SECURITY_WARN` on rejection. Calls `ResolveCredentials` internally. For OAuth2 credentials, checks the resolved token for CR/LF injection via `ICloudTaskExecutor::ContainsCrlf`, increments `ConnectorHttp::IncrementCredentialCrlfRejection()` and logs a security warning if found. Issues a `curl_easy_perform` GET to `{endpoint}/{container}?restype=container` with a 15-second timeout. Signs the request with `AzureSharedKeySigner::Sign` for Shared Key auth, or injects `Authorization: Bearer {token}` and `x-ms-version: 2024-11-04` for OAuth2. Returns `true` only when `CURLcode == CURLE_OK` and `HTTP status < 400`; on HTTP ≥ 400, appends up to 500 bytes of the response body to `errorMessage`.

- `static BuildEndpointUrl(connection) → std::string` — Pure utility. If `connection.m_Endpoint` is non-empty, returns it with any trailing slash stripped. Otherwise constructs `https://{account_name}.blob.core.windows.net` from `connection.m_Params["account_name"]`, falling back to the string `"unknown"` if the key is absent. Used both internally by `TestConnection` and externally (e.g., by task executors building per-operation URLs).

---

**Collaborators:**

- `ICloudConnector` (`cloud/cloudConnector.h`) — Abstract base. Defines `CloudConnection`, `CloudCredentials`, `CloudAuthType`, and `OAuth2ProviderInfo`. `AzureBlobConnector` inherits and overrides `GetType`, `TestConnection`, and `ResolveCredentials`; does not override `GetOAuth2ProviderInfo` (leaves it returning `false`).

- `KeyManager` (`keys/keyManager.h`) — Accessed via `Core::g_Core->GetKeyManager().GetCredential(m_KeyName)`. Owns all persisted credentials. `AzureBlobConnector` borrows a raw pointer from `KeyManager`; it must not be stored or used after the call returns.

- `OAuthTokenManager` (`keys/oauthTokenManager.h`) — Accessed via `Core::g_Core->GetOAuthTokenManager()`. Handles OAuth2 token refresh transparently; `AzureBlobConnector` only calls `GetAccessToken` and treats an empty result as failure.

- `ApiKeyCredential` / `BasicAuthCredential` (`keys/credential.h`) — Concrete credential types expected under `KeyManager`. Resolved via `dynamic_cast`; any other `ICredential` subtype causes explicit rejection.

- `AzureSharedKeySigner` (`cloud/azureSharedKeySigner.h`) — Produces the `Authorization: SharedKey` header and any required canonicalized headers (e.g., `x-ms-date`, `x-ms-version`, `Content-MD5`). Called only during `TestConnection`; callers constructing task-level requests call it directly.

- `SecretRedactor` (`log/secretRedactor.h`) — Global singleton. `AddSecret` is called on the raw account key so the value is scrubbed from all log output.

- `ConnectorHttp` (`cloud/connectorHttp.h`) — Provides `ValidatePublicHttpEndpoint`, `BoundedStringWriteCallback`, `ApplyHardenedDefaults`, and `IncrementCredentialCrlfRejection`. `ApplyHardenedDefaults` sets security-relevant curl options (e.g., SSL verification, redirect limits) on every handle created in `TestConnection`.

- `ICloudTaskExecutor` (`cloud/cloudTaskExecutor.h`) — Provides the static `ContainsCrlf` helper used to screen OAuth2 tokens before they are placed in HTTP headers.

- `Core::g_Core` (`core.h`, `engine.h`) — Global engine singleton; the only path to `KeyManager` and `OAuthTokenManager`.

- `libcurl` — Used directly in `TestConnection`. Each call initialises, uses, and cleans up its own `CURL*` handle; no shared handle or connection pool is involved at this layer.

---

**Threading / lifetime:**

`AzureBlobConnector` carries no mutable instance state; all methods are effectively stateless with respect to the object itself and are safe to call concurrently from multiple threads. However, they reach into `Core::g_Core` (global singleton) for `KeyManager` and `OAuthTokenManager` — callers must ensure `Core::g_Core` is fully initialised before invoking any method. The raw `ICredential*` pointer returned by `KeyManager::GetCredential` is borrowed for the duration of `ResolveCredentials` only and must not escape. `CloudCredentials` is produced on the stack by the caller and is not shared; it is the caller's responsibility to protect it after the call. `TestConnection` performs a synchronous blocking network call (up to 15 s); it must not be called on the engine's main event loop thread.

---

**Notes:**

- `BuildEndpointUrl` falls back to the literal string `"unknown"` in the hostname if `account_name` is missing from `m_Params`, producing the nonsense URL `https://unknown.blob.core.windows.net`. This does not fail loudly; callers relying on this function should pre-validate `account_name` themselves (as `TestConnection` does).

- The Shared Key branch in `ResolveCredentials` maps `credentials.m_SecretKey` to the account key and `credentials.m_AccessKeyId` to the account name — the reverse of the S3/SigV4 naming intuition where `AccessKeyId` is the key ID and `SecretKey` is the secret. This is intentional for `AzureSharedKeySigner`, which expects exactly that layout.

- The `SecretRedactor::AddSecret` call in `ResolveCredentials` is explicitly documented in the code as a likely no-op because `KeyManager`'s own `RegisterSecrets` path will have already registered the value. It is retained to cover hypothetical future paths (e.g., Azure SAS tokens sourced directly from `m_Params`) without requiring a second code review.

- The OAuth2 `x-ms-version: 2024-11-04` header is hardcoded in `TestConnection`. If Microsoft deprecates this API version, all OAuth2 connectivity tests will fail while Shared Key tests continue working, since the version header is injected by `AzureSharedKeySigner` in that path.

- HTTP response bodies are captured into a `std::string` via `ConnectorHttp::BoundedStringWriteCallback`. The "bounded" name implies a size cap enforced by the callback; `TestConnection` additionally truncates the error message append to 500 bytes itself, providing a second layer of protection against large XML error payloads from Azure appearing verbatim in logs or API responses.

- `AzureBlobConnector` does not override `GetOAuth2ProviderInfo`, so the default implementation in `ICloudConnector` returns `false`. The OAuth2 flow for Azure AD (device code, authorization code) must be configured via a separate connector or handled externally; `AzureBlobConnector` only consumes an already-resolved access token from `OAuthTokenManager`.

### 11_doc_application_cloud_cloudCircuitBreaker_h

<a id="11-doc-application-cloud-cloudcircuitbreaker-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/11_doc_application_cloud_cloudCircuitBreaker_h/docu.output.md`



## CloudCircuitBreaker

**Role:**  
`CloudCircuitBreaker` implements a per-connection circuit breaker for cloud service integrations in the j9t workflow engine. Its purpose is to detect and mitigate cascading failures (e.g., due to third-party cloud outages) by monitoring the success/failure rate of outbound requests for each named connection, automatically "opening" to block requests after repeated failures and then allowing probes to restore normal traffic when the dependency may have recovered. It implements the standard Closed → Open → HalfOpen → Closed failure-recovery state machine.

**Public API:**
- `CloudCircuitBreaker()` / `CloudCircuitBreaker(Config config)` — construct a circuit breaker, optionally with custom parameters (`failureThreshold`, `cooldownSeconds`, `halfOpenProbeCount`).
- `bool AllowRequest(const std::string& connectionName)`  
  Determines if a request should be permitted to proceed for the given connection. Returns `true` if allowed; `false` if short-circuited due to the circuit being open. Side effect: may transition connection state (Open → HalfOpen on cooldown expiry).
- `void RecordSuccess(const std::string& connectionName)`  
  Records a successful request for the given connection, resetting failure counters and transitioning the circuit to "Closed." Side effect: marks the connection as having ever succeeded (affects health reporting).
- `void RecordFailure(const std::string& connectionName)`  
  Records a failed request for the given connection. May increment the failure count, and potentially transition to "Open" if the threshold is reached or "Open" again if transitioning out of HalfOpen.
- `State GetState(const std::string& connectionName) const`  
  Returns the current state (`Closed`, `Open`, `HalfOpen`) of the named connection. Returns `Closed` if unknown.
- `static std::string StateToString(State state)`  
  Converts the internal state enum to a human-readable string.
- `std::vector<ConnectionHealth> GetHealthSummary() const`  
  Returns a vector of `ConnectionHealth` structs summarizing the state, consecutive failures, and if a connection has ever succeeded, for all connections tracked by the circuit breaker.
- `bool HasEverSucceeded(const std::string& connectionName) const`  
  Returns `true` if the named connection has ever recorded a successful request (via `RecordSuccess`).

**Collaborators:**  
- Uses standard library types: `std::unordered_map`, `std::vector`, `std::mutex`, `std::chrono`.
- Integrates with application logging macros/functions (`LOG_APP_INFO`, `LOG_APP_WARN`) for state transitions and events.
- Intended to work with the broader j9t engine, to gate and monitor cloud service connections (e.g., OpenAI, AWS, etc.).

**Threading / lifetime:**  
- Thread-safe for all public methods via an internal `std::mutex` (`m_Mutex`) that guards all circuit state and data structures (`m_Circuits`).  
- Caller does not own circuit objects; state for a connection is created on demand by passing a new `connectionName`.  
- `CloudCircuitBreaker` object should be held by the system for as long as connections need to be monitored. No special clean-up or destruction protocol is needed by clients.

**Notes:**
- The state machine is strictly implemented as:  
  - **Closed**: All requests allowed (unless enough consecutive failures occur).  
  - **Open**: All requests denied for a cooldown period.  
  - **HalfOpen**: A limited number of probes allowed — a probe request will close the circuit on success, re-open on failure.  
- Connection states are tracked independently by connection name string; there is no global breaker.
- All state transitions are logged to the application log (INFO and WARN).
- The `GetHealthSummary` and `HasEverSucceeded` methods are used for dashboard and monitoring purposes (e.g., UI indications).
- Unknown connections (never seen) are always reported as `Closed` state.
- Certain invariants:  
  - `m_EverSucceeded` is `true` only after at least one `RecordSuccess` call.  
  - Counters (`m_ConsecutiveFailures`, `m_HalfOpenProbes`) are reset on success or relevant state transitions.
- Behavior is strictly edge-triggered: failures only open circuits after the configured threshold, but not before, and open state persists for the configured cooldown regardless of further requests.

### 120_doc_engine_event_applicationEvent_h

<a id="120-doc-engine-event-applicationevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/120_doc_engine_event_applicationEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## AppErrorEvent

**Role:** `AppErrorEvent` is a concrete event class in the `AIAssistant` namespace that represents application-level error conditions surfaced through the engine's event system. It currently defines a single error code, `AppErrorBadCurl` (value 1000), which signals a libcurl failure. The class exists solely to carry a typed error code through the event bus so that listeners can distinguish application errors from other event categories without dynamic casting to unrelated types.

**Public API:**

- `AppErrorEvent(ErrorCode errorCode) → void` — Constructs the event with a specific `ErrorCode` enumerator. The only currently defined value is `AppErrorBadCurl = 1000`. No validation or side effects occur; the code is stored as-is.

- `GetErrorCode() const → int` — Returns the stored `ErrorCode` cast to `int`. Callers receive the raw integer value (e.g., `1000` for `AppErrorBadCurl`) rather than the enumerator, which allows downstream consumers to compare or log without needing a direct dependency on the `ErrorCode` enum.

- `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(AppError)` — Macro-generated static and virtual methods that identify this event's type token as `AppError`. Used by the event dispatcher for type-safe routing.

- `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryApp)` — Macro-generated method that tags this event as belonging to `EventCategoryApp`, enabling category-level filtering in the event system.

**Collaborators:**

- `event/event.h` — Provides the `Event` base class and the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` / `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros. The base class defines the virtual interface (type, category, name, handled flag) that the event dispatcher relies on. All routing and filtering logic lives there, not here.

- The event dispatcher (not directly included here) — Consumers register callbacks keyed on `AppError` type tokens; `AppErrorEvent` instances are routed to those callbacks by the dispatcher using the generated type methods.

**Threading / lifetime:**

`AppErrorEvent` instances are value-like objects with no heap-allocated members and no internal synchronization. Ownership follows whatever convention the broader event bus uses — typically the event is constructed on the stack or in a `unique_ptr`, dispatched synchronously, and destroyed immediately after dispatch. There is no reference counting or shared state internal to this class. Thread safety is entirely the responsibility of the enclosing event bus.

**Notes:**

- The `ErrorCode` enum starts at 1000, which suggests a deliberate namespace separation from other error-code ranges that other event or subsystem types may define. Adding new codes should continue in the 1000-series to avoid collisions.
- `GetErrorCode()` returns `int`, not `ErrorCode`, so callers doing comparisons must be careful: the implicit widening is fine, but equality checks against enumerator names require a cast back or a direct comparison against the integer literal.
- The class carries no message string, stack trace, or contextual detail beyond the code itself. Any richer diagnostic information must be logged by the site that constructs and dispatches the event before the event is created.

### 120_doc_engine_event_events_h

<a id="120-doc-engine-event-events-h"></a>

## eventForwardDecls.h

**Role:**  
This header file provides forward declarations and necessary includes for a standard set of event types used within the j9t workflow engine. These event types represent key system activities—application-level, filesystem-based, engine operations, timeline activities, and Python error reporting. Including this file ensures sources have type completeness for event handling and dispatch, while avoiding the cost of including full event class definitions unless required.

**Public API:**
- No functions, classes, or data members are defined in this file. Its sole purpose is to supply forward-declared types and include guards.

**Collaborators:**  
Relies on the following event header files, each of which contributes a major event type:
- `event/applicationEvent.h` — Defines ApplicationEvent type for application-scope notifications or requests.
- `event/filesystemEvent.h` — Defines FilesystemEvent for file monitoring, changes, and related triggers.
- `event/engineEvent.h` — Defines EngineEvent for internal workflow engine state or transitions.
- `event/timerEvent.h` — Defines TimerEvent for temporal triggers, delays, or time-based scheduling.
- `event/pythonErrorEvent.h` — Defines PythonErrorEvent to convey errors from embedded Python execution.

**Threading / lifetime:**  
This header is safe for any inclusion context; no objects are defined or owned here, and no threading or lifetime constraints apply. Actual event instance creation/ownership rules reside in the specific event classes referenced.

**Notes:**  
- Only type-level information is provided here; this header does not introduce any implementation or symbols on its own.
- Serves as a central place to import the j9t core event types, simplifying dependencies for modules that handle generic event dispatch or observation.
- Use this header instead of including each event file individually to maintain consistency across event-handling modules.

### 121_doc_engine_event_engineEvent_h

<a id="121-doc-engine-event-engineevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/121_doc_engine_event_engineEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## EngineEvent

**Role:** `EngineEvent` is a thin, strongly-typed event class within the `AIAssistant` namespace that represents lifecycle signals originating from the workflow engine itself. It extends the base `Event` type and currently defines a single engine-level signal, `EngineEventShutdown` (code 2000), which is used to notify subscribers that the engine is tearing down. The class plugs into the broader event dispatch infrastructure via the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` and `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros, which stamp it with a static type identifier and assign it to the `EventCategoryEngine` category bucket.

**Public API:**

- `EngineEvent(EngineEventCode engineEventCode)` — Constructs an engine event carrying the specified code. The only currently valid value is `EngineEventShutdown = 2000`. The code is stored as a private member; there are no heap allocations or side effects beyond member initialisation.

- `GetEngineCode() → int` — Returns the underlying integer value of the `EngineEventCode` enum stored in this instance. Callers receive a plain `int` rather than the enum type, so they must compare against the known constants (`EngineEventShutdown = 2000`) or cast back themselves.

- `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(EngineEvent)` — Macro-injected; provides static `GetStaticType()` and virtual `GetEventType()` methods used by the event dispatcher for type-based routing and filtering.

- `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryEngine)` — Macro-injected; provides `GetCategoryFlags()` returning the `EventCategoryEngine` bitmask, allowing category-level filtering in the event system without knowing the concrete type.

**Collaborators:**

- `event/event.h` — Defines the `Event` base class, the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` and `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros, and presumably the `EventCategoryEngine` category constant. The dispatch mechanism, listener registration, and event queue all live there or in adjacent files; callers who want to subscribe to engine events must interact with that infrastructure, not with this class directly.

**Threading / lifetime:**

`EngineEvent` instances are value-like and immutable after construction; all members are set in the constructor and exposed only through a `const` accessor. The class carries no shared state, no pointers, and no reference counts. If the event system dispatches events by pointer or reference, ownership follows whatever contract `Event` and the dispatcher establish — likely stack-allocated or short-lived heap objects consumed synchronously by the dispatch loop. Nothing in this file introduces additional threading constraints beyond those of the base `Event` type.

**Notes:**

- The `EngineEventCode` enum starts at 2000, which implies a deliberate numeric partitioning strategy across the event system — other event categories presumably occupy lower ranges. Any future engine event codes should continue from this range to avoid collisions.
- `GetEngineCode()` casts the enum to `int` on return, widening the API surface beyond the defined enum values. Callers should not treat arbitrary integers as valid engine codes; only values explicitly declared in `EngineEventCode` are meaningful.
- Because only `EngineEventShutdown` is currently defined, any switch or if-chain on the returned code is effectively a single-case check. New engine signals require adding entries to the `EngineEventCode` enum here and corresponding handling in all dispatch sites.

### 121_doc_engine_event_filesystemEvent_h

<a id="121-doc-engine-event-filesystemevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/121_doc_engine_event_filesystemEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## FileSystemEvent (and derived events)

**Role:**  
Defines the base event types for file system notifications within the AIAssistant workflow engine. These events represent and encapsulate occurrences of file addition, removal, or modification. This mechanism allows other components to react to specific file system changes in a decoupled, type-safe way using the engine's general event handling system.

**Public API:**

- `FileSystemEvent(std::string path)` — Constructs a file system event for the given file path. The `path` must be provided and is moved into the event for efficiency.
- `const std::string& GetPath() const` — Returns a reference to the (immutable) path associated with the event.

**For derived classes:**
- `FileAddedEvent(std::string path)` — Specialized event indicating a file was added at `path`. Inherits constructor from `FileSystemEvent`.
- `FileRemovedEvent(std::string path)` — Specialized event indicating a file was removed at `path`. Inherits constructor from `FileSystemEvent`.
- `FileModifiedEvent(std::string path)` — Specialized event indicating a file was modified at `path`. Inherits constructor from `FileSystemEvent`.

All derived event classes use `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` (e.g. `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(FileAdded)`) and `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryFileSys)` macros to declare their type and event category for run-time dispatch within the event system.

**Collaborators:**  
- Inherits from `AIAssistant::Event` (from "event/event.h"). All interactions (like dispatch, handling, and filtering) depend on the base `Event` infrastructure.
- Uses event type/category macros (`EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`, `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY`), which enable integration with the dispatch and classification system that routes events to interested listeners.

**Threading / lifetime:**  
- Events are constructed and typically owned by the code posting/publishing the event. Ownership follows standard event propagation semantics: the caller is responsible for the lifetime until dispatched; thereafter, ownership (and deletion) is controlled by the event system.
- The class is not explicitly thread-safe. Access to instances should conform to the threading/lifetime guarantees of the containing event queue or system. The path reference from `GetPath()` must not be cached beyond the event instance's lifetime.

**Notes:**  
- The file path is always stored as a `std::string` and is not checked for existence or validity; the event only records that a certain type of file system change occurred at that path.
- Events are strongly typed — ensure you match against the correct event subclass when handling.
- No automatic file system watching/tracking is performed here; this file only defines events, not their production.
- The class hierarchy is shallow and intended for extension only within the eventing system. Do not publicly subclass outside of workflow engine infrastructure unless you replicate the event macros required for registration and dispatch.
- The provided macros are assumed to be available via included headers. Misuse (e.g., subclassing without them) may cause broken event dispatch.

### 122_doc_engine_event_event_h

<a id="122-doc-engine-event-event-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/122_doc_engine_event_event_h/docu.output.md`



## Events.h — Event System Core

**Role:** This header defines the foundational event infrastructure used throughout the j9t workflow engine. It declares the `EventType` enumeration covering all observable occurrences in the system — from low-level input (keyboard, mouse) through file-system notifications (`FileAdded`, `FileRemoved`, `FileModified`), timer ticks, engine lifecycle signals, embedded Python failures (`PythonCrashed`), and the four-phase AI dispatch lifecycle (`AiCallStarted`, `AiCallRetrying`, `AiCallCompleted`, `AiCallFailed`). It also provides the `Event` abstract base class, the `EventDispatcher` type-safe routing helper, and two convenience macros (`EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`, `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY`) that concrete event subclasses use to satisfy the polymorphic interface with minimal boilerplate.

**Public API:**

- `Event::IsHandled() const → bool` — Returns the current handled flag. Once `true`, the engine's propagation loop should treat the event as consumed and stop routing it further.
- `Event::SetHandled(bool handled = true) → void` — Marks or unmarks the event as handled. Called directly or indirectly through `EventDispatcher::Dispatch`. Setting this inside a handler short-circuits downstream listeners.
- `Event::GetEventType() const → EventType` — Pure virtual; concrete subclasses implement via `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`. Returns the discriminator used by `EventDispatcher` to match handlers.
- `Event::GetName() const → const char*` — Pure virtual; concrete subclasses return a string literal (the enumerator name via `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`). Intended for logging and diagnostics only.
- `Event::GetCategoryFlags() const → int` — Pure virtual; returns a bitmask of `EventCategory` values. Concrete subclasses implement via `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY`.
- `Event::IsInCategory(EventCategory category) const → bool` — Checks whether the event belongs to a given category using bitwise AND against `GetCategoryFlags()`. Useful for broad filtering (e.g., "is this any AI event?") without knowing the precise `EventType`.
- `Event::ToString() const → std::string` — Virtual; default returns `GetName()`. Subclasses may override to include payload details for richer log output.
- `EventDispatcher::EventDispatcher(Event& event)` — Constructs a dispatcher bound to a specific event instance. Does not take ownership; the referenced `Event` must outlive the dispatcher.
- `EventDispatcher::Dispatch<T>(EventFn<T> func) → bool` — Compares `m_Event.GetEventType()` against `T::GetStaticType()`. If they match, downcasts the stored `Event&` to `T&` via `static_cast` and invokes `func`, storing the returned `bool` in `m_Event.m_Handled`. Returns `true` if the type matched (regardless of the handler's return value), `false` if the types did not match. The `bool` return of the handler itself is what sets the handled flag.

**Collaborators:**

- Concrete event subclasses (not present in this file) must use `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` and `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` to satisfy the pure-virtual interface; `EventDispatcher::Dispatch` relies on the `GetStaticType()` static method that the macro injects.
- The engine's event loop or event bus (not shown here) constructs `EventDispatcher` per event and calls `Dispatch` for each registered handler.
- The AI dispatch layer emits `AiCallStarted / AiCallRetrying / AiCallCompleted / AiCallFailed` events under `EventCategoryAi`; listeners can filter for all of them with `IsInCategory(EventCategoryAi)`.
- The file-watcher subsystem emits `FileAdded`, `FileRemoved`, and `FileModified` under `EventCategoryFileSys`.
- The embedded Python runtime signals crashes via `PythonCrashed` under `EventCategoryEngine`.

**Threading / lifetime:**

- `Event` instances are not synchronized internally. `m_Handled` is a plain `bool` with no atomic protection; callers must ensure that a single `Event` object is not dispatched concurrently from multiple threads.
- `EventDispatcher` holds a non-owning reference to the `Event` passed at construction. The `Event` must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the `EventDispatcher` — typically both are stack-allocated within the same dispatch call frame, making lifetime trivially safe in the common pattern.
- `EventFn<T>` is a `std::function`, so captured lambdas that reference external state must manage that state's lifetime independently.

**Notes:**

- `EventDispatcher::Dispatch` uses `static_cast`, not `dynamic_cast`. The type safety guarantee rests entirely on `GetStaticType()` returning a value that uniquely identifies the concrete class. Two unrelated concrete types must never share the same `EventType` enumerator or the cast will produce undefined behaviour.
- The `m_Handled` flag on `Event` is write-accessible via `SetHandled`, which is public. Any code with a reference to the event can mark it handled without going through the dispatcher; keep this in mind when debugging premature event suppression.
- `EventCategory` uses a plain `enum` (not `enum class`), so its enumerators are visible in the `AIAssistant` namespace without qualification. This is intentional for use in bitwise expressions but means new category names must be chosen carefully to avoid collisions.
- `ToString()` includes `<sstream>` in the header. Subclasses that override `ToString()` for richer output already have `std::ostringstream` available without an additional include.

### 122_doc_engine_event_keyboardEvent_h

<a id="122-doc-engine-event-keyboardevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/122_doc_engine_event_keyboardEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## KeyPressedEvent

**Role:**  
`KeyPressedEvent` represents a discrete keyboard keypress event within the AIAssistant event handling subsystem. It encapsulates which character key was pressed and provides a typed interface for dispatch to listeners interested in keyboard interactions during workflow or UI operations.

**Public API:**
- `explicit KeyPressedEvent(char key)` — Constructor. Takes the pressed key as a `char` and constructs the event instance.
- `char GetKey() const` — Returns the character key associated with this event. No side effects.
- `std::string ToString() const override` — Returns a textual representation (e.g., `"KeyPressedEvent: a"`) of the event for logging or debugging.
- `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(KeyPressed)` — Expands to a function for runtime event type identification (macro from base event system).
- `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryKeyboard)` — Expands to a function for runtime event category identification, labeling this event as belonging to keyboard-related events (macro from base event system).

**Collaborators:**  
- Inherits from `Event` (declared in `"event/event.h"`), so interacts with the event polling/dispatch system that expects base-class pointers or references.
- Integrates with systems or handlers processing keyboard input events under the `AIAssistant` namespace.

**Threading / lifetime:**  
- `KeyPressedEvent` instances are expected to be stack-allocated or managed as part of an event dispatch flow. There are no internal resources or thread synchronization; ownership and concurrency constraints depend on the surrounding event loop implementation.
- Callers are responsible for not modifying or deleting the event while it may still be in use by event listeners.

**Notes:**  
- `m_Key` is a `char`; only single-byte (likely ASCII) keys are represented. Multibyte or Unicode keypresses are not supported in this class.
- The actual event-type and category macros (e.g., `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`, `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY`) rely on the implementation of the event base system and may influence dynamic dispatch and filtering. If you add further event listeners/categories, coordinate with the event system’s infrastructure.

### 123_doc_engine_event_eventQueue_h

<a id="123-doc-engine-event-eventqueue-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/123_doc_engine_event_eventQueue_h/docu.output.md`



## EventQueue

**Role:** `EventQueue` is the central message bus that decouples multi-threaded producers from the single-threaded main loop inside `AIAssistant`. Any subsystem — keyboard input, file watcher, AI request pool, Python engine, web server, or signal-flag checking in `Core::CheckSignalFlags` — can push typed `Event` objects onto the queue from any thread. `Core::Run` drains the queue once per loop iteration and dispatches the resulting batch, keeping all event processing on the main thread while leaving producers completely free of main-thread coupling.

**Public API:**

- `Push(EventPtr event) → void` — Appends a heap-allocated `Event` (wrapped in `std::shared_ptr`) to the back of the internal `std::queue`. Takes ownership of the pointer via `std::move`; the caller's `shared_ptr` is left empty after the call. Acquires `m_QueueAccessMutex` for the duration of the push. Safe to call from any thread at any time, including before `Core::Run` has started.

- `PopAll() → std::vector<EventPtr>` — Atomically swaps the internal queue with a local empty queue (holding the lock only for the `std::swap`), then moves every element from the local queue into a `std::vector` outside the lock, and returns the vector. After the call the internal queue is empty. Vector construction, element movement, and eventual `shared_ptr` destruction for any events that are discarded all occur outside the critical section, so producers are not blocked by the caller's processing time.

**Collaborators:**

- `AIAssistant::Event` (`event/event.h`) — The polymorphic base type stored in the queue. `EventQueue` itself has no knowledge of concrete event subtypes; dispatch logic lives in `Core::Run`.
- `Core::Run` — The sole intended consumer; calls `PopAll()` once per main-loop iteration and dispatches the returned batch.
- `Core::CheckSignalFlags`, `keyboardInput`, `fileWatcher`, `aiRequestPool`, `pythonEngine`, `webServer` — All act as producers by calling `Push()` from their respective threads.

**Threading / lifetime:**

`EventQueue` is designed for the **multiple-producer / single-consumer (MPSC)** pattern. `Push` is fully thread-safe and may be called concurrently from any number of threads. `PopAll` is **not** safe for concurrent consumers; only one thread (the main loop) must ever call it. `EventQueue` itself has no internal thread or condition variable — it does not wake the main loop; the main loop polls it. The object must outlive all producers; in practice it is owned by `Core` and lives for the duration of the process. Because events are `std::shared_ptr`, a producer that retains its own copy of the pointer after pushing will keep the `Event` alive even after the main thread drains and drops it.

**Notes:**

- The swap-then-drain pattern in `PopAll` means the mutex is held for O(1) time regardless of queue depth. This is intentional — long event-processing work on the main thread does not starve concurrent producers.
- There is no capacity limit or backpressure mechanism. If the main loop stalls, producers will continue to accumulate events unbounded in memory.
- `PopAll` returning an empty vector is a normal, non-error condition when no events have arrived since the last drain.
- Because `EventPtr` is a `shared_ptr`, the reference count is decremented (and the `Event` may be destroyed) when the returned vector goes out of scope on the main thread, not at push time. Producers that share ownership via `shared_ptr` copies will observe the object staying alive until both sides release it.
- The `mutable` qualifier on `m_QueueAccessMutex` is present in the header but neither `Push` nor `PopAll` is declared `const`, so `mutable` has no practical effect in the current API surface.

The `PythonCrashedEvent` class represents an event signaling that the embedded Python interpreter or environment has crashed within the AI Assistant component of the j9t workflow engine. - `const std::string& GetMessage() const` — Returns a constant reference to the descriptive message originally passed to the constructor. Use this to access error context for logging, reporting, or UI display.
- `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(PythonCrashed)` — Macro that injects code identifying this class as an event of type `PythonCrashed`. Used for run-time event dispatch and filtering.
- `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryEngine)` — Macro that marks this event as belonging to the "Engine" category, aiding in event routing and diagnostics.

- Inherits from `Event` (from `event/event.h`), which defines the base event interface and mechanics for the engine's event-handling subsystem.

- **Fix:** Sanitize or escape user-controlled values (including file paths) before logging/output. Never allow user input to directly appear in structured logs.

- **Issue:** Full file paths and possibly internal configuration values are printed to stderr and log files.
- **Impact:** If error logs or console output are exposed to end-users or attackers (e.g., in a shared environment, log collection, or bug reports), they may disclose sensitive information about internal file system structure or configuration.
- **Fix:** Avoid exposing full path information or sensitive configuration in error messages or logs. Instead, provide generic error messages and log more detailed info only in secure, access-controlled locations.

### 124_doc_engine_event_events_h

<a id="124-doc-engine-event-events-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/124_doc_engine_event_events_h/docu.output.md`



## event.h (Aggregate Event Header)

**Role:** This is a convenience umbrella header that aggregates all event-type headers used by the j9t workflow engine into a single include. It provides no declarations of its own; its sole purpose is to allow consumers to pull in the complete set of engine event types — application, filesystem, engine, timer, and Python error events — with one `#include "event.h"` directive rather than five separate includes.

**Public API:**

This file declares no classes, functions, or variables. All public API surface is provided by the included headers:

- `event/applicationEvent.h` — application-lifecycle events (startup, shutdown, and similar top-level state transitions).
- `event/filesystemEvent.h` — filesystem watch events, surfaced when the file watcher detects changes on monitored paths.
- `event/engineEvent.h` — core workflow engine events, covering request dispatch, pipeline state changes, or similar internal engine signals.
- `event/timerEvent.h` — timer-fired events, used by scheduled or delayed workflow steps.
- `event/pythonErrorEvent.h` — events emitted when the embedded Python interpreter encounters an error, allowing the engine to react to or log Python-side failures.

**Collaborators:** Any subsystem that needs to handle or dispatch more than one event category should include this header rather than individual event headers. The workflow engine core, webhook handlers, file watchers, timer subsystem, and Python integration layer all produce event types covered by the headers gathered here.

**Threading / lifetime:** No objects are defined here; lifetime and threading rules are governed entirely by the individual event type definitions in the included headers. Readers should consult those files for ownership semantics of specific event objects.

**Notes:** Because this is a `#pragma once` guarded aggregate header, adding a new event category to the engine requires a corresponding inclusion here to keep the umbrella complete. The absence of a new event type from this file will silently leave callers that rely solely on this header without visibility into that type — a maintenance invariant that must be enforced manually.

## TimerElapsedEvent

**Role:**  
`TimerElapsedEvent` is a concrete event class within the `AIAssistant` namespace representing the expiration of a timer. When a timer managed by the workflow or event system elapses, an instance of this event is created and typically dispatched to notify interested components that the specific timer has completed. It carries the timer's unique identifier for downstream handling.

**Public API:**
- `TimerElapsedEvent(int timerID)` — Constructs a `TimerElapsedEvent` with the provided timer ID. `timerID` is an integer uniquely identifying which timer triggered the event.
- `int GetTickId() const` — Returns the timer ID associated with this event. This allows event handlers to determine which timer has elapsed.
- `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(TimerElapsed)` — Macro expands to declare the event's concrete type for event system dispatch and filtering.
- `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryTimer)` — Macro expands to assign the event category, facilitating categorization and dispatch filtering.

**Collaborators:**  
- Inherits from `AIAssistant::Event` (declared in "event/event.h"), which provides the interface and polymorphic event base for the event-dispatching mechanism.  
- Intended to be processed by components that observe or subscribe to timer-related events in the system.  
- Uses system-defined event macros (e.g. `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`, `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY`) recognized by the event infrastructure.

**Threading / lifetime:**  
- Ownership is typical for event objects: generally heap-allocated by the timer or event dispatcher, passed by pointer or reference within the event system, and destroyed after dispatch/handling.
- No internal synchronization; the class itself is plain data and not thread-safe for mutation, but is safe for concurrent read access.
- Caller/owner is responsible for ensuring that the event object remains valid for as long as needed by any event handlers receiving it.

**Notes:**  
- The only payload is the integer timer ID (`m_TimerID`), meaning all discrimination between timers must occur via this value in handlers.
- No additional time data (e.g., actual tick time) is stored; only the originating timer's ID.
- Macros (`EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`, `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY`) must be recognized and honored by the event system for correct operation. These likely affect RTTI, filtering, or signal/slot linkage.
- There are no virtual or override functions in the provided snippet, but proper polymorphic interaction is assumed via the `Event` base class.  
- No copy/move/assignment restrictions are stated. The class is lightweight (holds a single int).

### 124_doc_engine_json_configParser_h

<a id="124-doc-engine-json-configparser-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/124_doc_engine_json_configParser_h/docu.output.md`



### HIGH Information Disclosure of Sensitive TLS and Secret Fields in Logs
- **Location:** `ConfigParser::Parse` and `ConfigParser::ParseInterfaces` (various, e.g., line ~190, ~422, ~594)
- **Issue:** Sensitive values such as `TlsCert`, `TlsKey`, `keys_file`, `mcp_keys_file`, `TrustedProxyHeader`, and `TrustedRoleHeader` are logged in plaintext via LOG_CORE_INFO when parsed from the config.
- **Impact:** If logs are accessible to unauthorized parties, certificate material, key paths, or header-based trust secrets could be leaked, compromising TLS, authentication, and potentially giving attackers information for privilege escalation or MITM.
- **Fix:** Do not log the actual value of sensitive configuration items such as `TlsCert`, `TlsKey`, or any field that points to cryptographic secrets or trust indicators. Log only whether the field was set, its length, or that it was present, e.g., `LOG_CORE_INFO("TlsCert: [REDACTED] ({} bytes present)", engineConfig.m_TlsCert.size());`

---

### MEDIUM Unvalidated Path Input Enables Path Traversal
- **Location:** `ConfigParser::Parse`, assignment of `m_QueueFolderFilepath`, `m_WorkflowsFolderFilepath`, `m_KeysFilePath`, and `m_McpKeysFilePath` (lines ~166, ~172, ~230, ~361)
- **Issue:** Configuration file values are assigned directly to file path fields with no validation or restriction on the path (e.g., no check for relative paths, absolute paths, or access outside intended directories).
- **Impact:** A malicious config could set these to `../../etc/passwd` or similar, potentially leading to read/write outside the intended directory sandbox, especially if later code uses the fields unsafely.
- **Fix:** Implement path validation/sanitization before using/assigning any path in configuration. Ensure only allowed directories are accepted, and restrict usage of `..`, absolute paths, and symbolic links.

---

### MEDIUM No Enforcement of Numeric or Resource Limits in Configuration
- **Location:** `ConfigParser::Parse` (multiple, e.g., `max_threads`, `max_inflight_ai_calls`, `python_engines`, etc. ~178, ~325, ~353, ~370)
- **Issue:** Numeric values from config are assigned to resource-controlling fields (thread counts, inflight requests, Python engines, request body size, etc.) with little or no range checking (except `port` and `session_timeout_hours`).
- **Impact:** An attacker with control over the config can force the engine into allocating huge resources, causing uncontrolled memory, thread, or file creation, and leading to Denial of Service.
- **Fix:** Add reasonable upper and lower bounds to all such settings. For example, cap `max_threads` to a sane maximum (like 256), `maxInflightAiCalls`, `MaxRequestBodyMB`, etc. If exceeded, either fail parsing or clamp to defaults.

---

### LOW Use of Exception (catching all simdjson errors as warnings) May Obscure Malformed Input
- **Location:** `ConfigParser::Parse` (catch block near line ~412)
- **Issue:** For unknown fields in config, the code tries to stringify/log them, and on failure logs a warning, but parsing overall will succeed.
- **Impact:** Malformed or malicious input could be ignored, and unintended or invalid fields could silently pass, potentially opening avenue for confusion or deserialization vulnerabilities elsewhere.
- **Fix:** Consider treating unknown or unserializable fields as a parse failure, or introducing a stricter validation mode where unknown fields are flagged as errors.

---

### LOW No TLS Key/Certificate Validation Before Usage
- **Location:** `ConfigParser::Parse` lines ~287, ~294
- **Issue:** No check is performed to ensure values for `TlsCert` and `TlsKey` are not empty, are in valid PEM format, or refer to existing files.
- **Impact:** If left misconfigured, the server may start with invalid or missing TLS credentials, enabling downgrade or loss of encrypted channel.
- **Fix:** After assignment, check the field for reasonable content (e.g., file exists, contains valid certificate/private key), and fail config parse if invalid.

---

### LOW Potential JSON Injection in Logs
- **Location:** Logging of unescaped and unchecked config field values, e.g., `LOG_CORE_INFO("name: {}", name);` in `ParseInterfaces`.
- **Issue:** Arbitrary values from config files are logged without any sanitization or truncation.
- **Impact:** Malicious configuration could inject log lines, potentially confusing log parsers or, if logs are ingested elsewhere, enable log injection attacks.
- **Fix:** Sanitize input before logging by escaping control characters, limiting length, or using structured logging with explicit encoding.

---

### NONE
No memory safety, concurrency, cryptographic primitives, SSRF, injection, or insecure deserialization vulnerabilities were found within the present code. However, the issues above warrant attention.

### 125_doc_engine_event_filesystemEvent_h

<a id="125-doc-engine-event-filesystemevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/125_doc_engine_event_filesystemEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## FileSystemEvents (event/filesystemevent.h)

**Role:** Defines the three concrete file-system event types used by j9t's file-watching subsystem — `FileAddedEvent`, `FileRemovedEvent`, and `FileModifiedEvent`. All three derive from the intermediate `FileSystemEvent` base, which itself derives from `AIAssistant::Event`, carrying a single file-system path as their payload. These events are constructed by whatever component detects file-system changes and are dispatched through the engine's central event bus so that subscribers (secrets reloading, config watchers, workflow triggers, etc.) can react to specific file-system activity.

**Public API:**

- `FileSystemEvent(std::string path)` — Constructs the base with the affected file-system path; ownership of the string is taken by move. All three concrete types inherit this constructor via `using FileSystemEvent::FileSystemEvent`.
- `GetPath() const → const std::string&` — Returns the absolute or relative path associated with the event. The reference is valid for the lifetime of the event object.
- `FileAddedEvent` — Signals that a new file appeared at `GetPath()`. Stamped with type `FileAdded` and category `EventCategoryFileSys` via the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` / `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros.
- `FileRemovedEvent` — Signals that a file at `GetPath()` was deleted. Same category.
- `FileModifiedEvent` — Signals that an existing file at `GetPath()` was written to or otherwise changed. Same category.

**Collaborators:**

- `AIAssistant::Event` (event/event.h) — The polymorphic base class for the entire event system. Provides the type-identification and category infrastructure consumed by the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` and `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros; callers querying event type or category should use the interface from that header.
- `EventCategoryFileSys` — A category bitmask declared in `event/event.h` (or a companion categories header) that allows category-based filtering in the event dispatcher.
- File-watching subsystem — Whichever component monitors the OS file-system (inotify, FSEvents, ReadDirectoryChangesW, or a polling loop) is the producer of these events. That component is responsible for constructing and posting the appropriate subclass.

**Threading / lifetime:**

Event objects are typically short-lived value types allocated by the producer, dispatched synchronously or queued to the event bus, and destroyed after all handlers have run. Because `m_Path` is a plain `std::string` member there is no shared ownership. If the event bus queues events across threads the producer must ensure the event object outlives the queue entry; posting by value (or `unique_ptr`) is the safe pattern. No internal synchronization is present in these classes.

**Notes:**

- The `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` macro must assign a unique `EventType` enumerator (`FileAdded`, `FileRemoved`, `FileModified`) in the central `EventType` enum; if those enumerators are missing the file will not compile.
- `EventCategoryFileSys` is a bitmask category, so a single dispatcher filter can match all three subtypes without knowing their concrete type.
- There is no recursive-rename or move event here; if the file-watching backend detects a rename it must synthesize a `FileRemovedEvent` for the old path and a `FileAddedEvent` for the new path, or the move will go unrepresented.
- The path string is stored verbatim as provided by the producer; there is no normalization, canonicalization, or existence check inside these classes.

### 125_doc_engine_input_keyboardInput_h

<a id="125-doc-engine-input-keyboardinput-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/125_doc_engine_input_keyboardInput_h/docu.output.md`



## KeyboardInput

**Role:**  
`KeyboardInput` is responsible for listening for keyboard input (non-blocking, in the background) on both Windows and POSIX platforms. It detects keypresses from standard input, creates key events on user press, requests engine shutdown when 'q' or 'Q' is pressed, and injects these events into the workflow engine's central event queue. It is typically started and stopped by higher-level engine components.

**Public API:**
- `KeyboardInput()` / `~KeyboardInput()` — Default constructor and destructor; resource cleanup is handled automatically via RAII.
- `void Start()` — Begins listening for keyboard input asynchronously. No arguments. This launches the listener in the engine thread pool using `Core::g_Core->GetThreadPool().SubmitTask(...)`. Safe to call multiple times; only the first call actually starts the thread.
- `void Stop()` — Stops listening. Returns immediately unless there is an active listening task, in which case the method blocks until the listener thread finishes. Multiple calls are safe. Also logs shutdown info.

**Collaborators:**
- `Core::g_Core` — Singleton providing global access to engine facilities such as event queue, thread pool (`GetThreadPool()`), and shutdown signaling (`RequestQuit()`).
- `ThreadPool::SubmitTask` — Used to run the listener in the background.
- `EngineEvent`, `KeyPressedEvent` (via `event/keyboardEvent.h` and `event/events.h`) — Created and posted via `Core::g_Core->PushEvent()` to communicate key presses and shutdown intention to the engine event system.
- Platform-specific concurrency and input headers (`<unistd.h>`, `<conio.h>`, `select`, `getchar`, `_kbhit`, `_getch`).

**Threading / lifetime:**
- `KeyboardInput` is non-copyable, non-movable due to the presence of `std::atomic` and `std::future` fields (although not explicitly deleted).
- Calls to `Start()`/`Stop()` are expected to be externally synchronized if used from multiple threads.
- Listener task is run asynchronously on the engine thread pool. `m_Running` is an atomic flag protecting orderly startup/shutdown.
- Destructor itself does not call `Stop()`. Caller must stop the listener before destroying the object to avoid a dangling thread.
- The listener exits promptly after `Stop()` sets `m_Running` to false.

**Notes:**
- On POSIX systems, if `stdin` is not a TTY (`isatty(STDIN_FILENO)` returns false, e.g., in non-interactive Docker containers), keyboard input is disabled and no events are generated.
- Terminal echo and buffering are assumed to already be managed by a higher-level `TerminalManager`, as per code comments. The input is read in non-blocking mode using either `select()` (POSIX) or polling with sleep (`_kbhit()`/`_getch()`, Windows).
- Only printable key presses are passed as `KeyPressedEvent`s, filtering out newlines and EOF on POSIX.
- When the user presses 'q' or 'Q', the global engine will receive an EngineEventShutdown event, and a synchronous `RequestQuit()` is called.
- The component relies heavily on core engine singletons and event-driven design; it does not own any resources except for its own background task.
- Designed to be robust against repeated `Start()` or `Stop()` calls, and safely shuts down listeners.
- Sleep/polling interval is hard-coded to 100ms; keypresses may be detected up to 100ms after actual press.

This class is intended for internal engine use: UI modules or workflow steps may "listen" for keypresses only via events, never by querying `KeyboardInput` directly.

### LOW Potential Incomplete JSON String Escaping
- **Location:** JsonHelper::SanitizeForJson (approx. lines 19–60)
- **Issue:** The SanitizeForJson function appears to intend escaping text for safe JSON embedding, but it does not cover all control characters and does not perform UTF-8 or Unicode escaping for non-printable or special characters (\b, \f, and others), nor does it escape forward slashes or non-ASCII data. There is also a redundant `case ''` that serves no purpose.
- **Impact:** Malformed or unexpected JSON may be produced in edge cases, possibly enabling attackers to manipulate JSON structure (rare in practice but dangerous if assumptions are made downstream), or to inject control characters that could affect some parsers. Downstream logic expecting proper JSON may handle input unsafely or fail with unexpected structure, depending on usage.
- **Fix:** Use a well-tested JSON library for escaping (such as nlohmann::json or rapidjson). If hand-writing, add all required string escapes per RFC 8259, including \b, \f, and escaping control codes as `\u00XX` for chars < 0x20. Remove the `case ''` statement.

### 126_doc_engine_event_keyboardEvent_h

<a id="126-doc-engine-event-keyboardevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/126_doc_engine_event_keyboardEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## KeyPressedEvent

**Role:** `KeyPressedEvent` is a concrete event class within the `AIAssistant` namespace that represents a single keyboard key-press occurrence in the engine's event system. It inherits from `Event` and carries exactly one piece of payload — the character that was pressed — making it the typed signal that input-handling subsystems consume when a key stroke is detected.

**Public API:**

- `KeyPressedEvent(char key)` — explicit single-argument constructor; stores the pressed character in `m_Key`. No side effects; no heap allocation beyond the object itself.
- `GetKey() const → char` — returns the character associated with the key-press. Read-only; no side effects.
- `ToString() const → std::string` — produces a human-readable description in the form `"KeyPressedEvent: <char>"`. Intended for logging and debug output. Overrides `Event::ToString`.
- `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(KeyPressed)` — macro expansion (defined in `event/event.h`) that injects `GetEventType()`, `GetName()`, and `GetStaticType()` returning the `EventType::KeyPressed` discriminator.
- `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryKeyboard)` — macro expansion that injects `GetCategoryFlags()` returning the `EventCategoryKeyboard` bitmask, allowing category-based event filtering.

**Collaborators:**

- `event/event.h` — provides the `Event` base class, the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` and `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros, and the `EventType` / `EventCategory` enumerations that this class plugs into. The behaviour of type dispatch and category filtering is entirely determined there.
- Any event dispatcher or event bus in the broader engine that routes events by `EventType::KeyPressed` or filters by `EventCategoryKeyboard` will consume instances of this class.

**Threading / lifetime:**

`KeyPressedEvent` objects are plain value-semantic structs with no internal synchronisation. Ownership and lifetime are entirely the caller's responsibility. The class contains no virtual destructor of its own, so callers must ensure they do not delete a `KeyPressedEvent` through an `Event*` base pointer unless `Event` itself declares a virtual destructor (verify in `event/event.h`). Instances are typically short-lived: created at the point of input capture, dispatched synchronously or queued, then discarded.

**Notes:**

- The key payload is typed as `char`, which means it carries only 8-bit ASCII values. Extended keys (function keys, arrow keys, modifier-only presses) are not representable and would require a separate event type or a wider key-code type.
- There is no repeat count or modifier-state (Shift, Ctrl, Alt) stored on this event. If the engine needs to distinguish a held key from a new press, or modified characters from bare ones, that information must come from a different event type or an extended version of this class.
- The `explicit` constructor prevents accidental implicit conversion from `char` to `KeyPressedEvent`, which is the correct defensive choice when passing events through generic handlers.

### 126_doc_engine_json_configChecker_h

<a id="126-doc-engine-json-configchecker-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/126_doc_engine_json_configChecker_h/docu.output.md`



## ConfigChecker

**Role:**  
The `ConfigChecker` class is responsible for validating and normalizing the runtime configuration for the AI workflow engine. It ensures required directories exist, key API and engine parameters are set, and fields are within sane ranges, updating `EngineConfig` as needed. Errors are logged in detail, and recoverable configuration issues are automatically fixed where possible.

**Public API:**
- `ConfigChecker()` — default constructor; creates a stateless checker object.
- `~ConfigChecker()` — default destructor.
- `bool Check(ConfigParser::EngineConfig& engineConfig)`  
  Validates the fields of the provided `EngineConfig` instance (passed by non-const ref). Ensures configured directories exist, API interface(s) are valid, and key integer parameters (like number of threads, file sizes, Python engines, inflight AI calls, and sleep durations) are set within documented bounds, clamping or fixing where necessary. Updates both `engineConfig` and internal state. Logs and prints to stderr on any failures. Returns `true` if all requirements are satisfied (or were fixed); `false` if any critical errors remain.
- `bool ConfigIsOk() const`  
  Returns whether the last call to `Check()` found (or fixed) a valid configuration (`true`) or not.

**Collaborators:**
- Uses `ConfigParser::EngineConfig` (from `json/configParser.h`) as the configuration data structure for validation and normalization.
- Uses `EngineCore::IsDirectory` to check filesystem paths for queue and workflow folders.
- Uses logging macros such as `LOG_CORE_ERROR`, `LOG_APP_ERROR` and the C stdlib `fprintf` for logging and direct user feedback.
- Depends on some constants/enums (e.g., `ConfigParser::EngineConfig::InterfaceType`) and utility classes from the broader engine, especially for structure fields and parsing responsibility.

**Threading / lifetime:**
- `ConfigChecker` is designed for single-threaded use; no internal locking or atomic updates are present.
- The caller owns both the `ConfigChecker` instance and the `EngineConfig` object whose reference is passed to `Check()`.
- `Check()` mutates fields of `EngineConfig` in place (e.g., clamping/fixing values and setting `m_ConfigValid`), so no concurrent use on the same config object is supported or intended.
- No background or asynchronous activity is started by this class.

**Notes:**
- `Check()` not only validates but also silently **fixes** certain misconfigurations (such as out-of-range or missing values for thread count, sleep timer, file size, max inflight calls, and Python engine instances), logging the changes and setting them to sane defaults.
- Key required directories (`m_QueueFolderFilepath` and `m_WorkflowsFolderFilepath`) must exist as directories; otherwise, errors are logged and `false` is returned.
- The selected API interface (`m_ApiInterfaces` at `m_ApiIndex`) must exist and be valid, with a proper `https://` URL and non-empty model string.
- If any check fails, an error is both logged and printed on stderr for operator visibility.
- After all checks, the `m_ConfigValid` member in `EngineConfig` is always updated to reflect success/failure.
- There is no exception propagation; all reporting is via return value, logging, and mutations of the config object.
- Behavior is idempotent (calling `Check()` multiple times with the same config yields the same result and logs).
- Port range validation is delegated to the parser, not checked here.  
- Some resource-related fields (`m_MaxInflightAiCalls`, `m_PythonEngines`) are clamped to hard-coded limits to prevent excessive load or runaway resource use.  
- No other side effects outside config mutation and log/console output.

### 126_doc_engine_keys_credential_h

<a id="126-doc-engine-keys-credential-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/126_doc_engine_keys_credential_h/docu.output.md`



### HIGH Hardcoded Secrets and Insecure Storage
- **Location:** Classes ApiKeyCredential, OAuthCredential, KeyPairCredential, BasicAuthCredential (lines ~19–63)
- **Issue:** Secrets such as API keys, OAuth tokens, private keys, and passwords are stored as plain std::string members. There is no evidence of secure memory management (e.g., zeroization on destruction), nor any encryption at rest or in memory. Storing sensitive values directly in heap-allocated std::string may leave secrets in memory after use, subject to swapping, core dumps, or leaks.
- **Impact:** Secrets may be exposed through memory dumps, swap files, or process inspection, increasing risk of credential theft.
- **Fix:** Use a secure memory container that zeroizes memory upon release for all secrets (e.g., a custom secure_string or OS-provided facilities). Consider encrypting credentials at rest, and avoid unnecessary long-lived secrets in memory.

### MEDIUM - Potential Secret Leakage via Serialization or Logging
- **Location:** ICredential and subclasses (lines ~19–63)
- **Issue:** All credential fields are public or accessible from outside, and GetType is intended for serialization. If subclasses are serialized or logged directly, secrets may be exposed. The code gives no indication of redaction or filtering during logging/serialization.
- **Impact:** API keys, passwords, and private keys could be leaked in logs, error outputs, or when debugging.
- **Fix:** Implement secret redaction and avoid including sensitive fields in serialization or logging routines. Specifically, do not serialize or log sensitive fields unless explicitly required, and document/redact accordingly.

### LOW - No Integrity/Authentication Mechanism for Credentials
- **Location:** All credential classes
- **Issue:** The interface does not specify any means of validating, checking integrity, or authenticating that the stored credential is correct, unaltered, or associated with a specific user/session.
- **Impact:** Credentials may be tampered with in memory if an attacker achieves code execution in the process, or during (de)serialization if used elsewhere.
- **Fix:** Consider tighter access controls, and use structures that support memory authentication where necessary.

---

If this file is used strictly as a data definition layer and not responsible for transport/serialization/deserialization or logging, these issues may be mitigated elsewhere. However, these design choices are inherently risky for secret handling.

### 127_doc_engine_event_pythonErrorEvent_h

<a id="127-doc-engine-event-pythonerrorevent-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/127_doc_engine_event_pythonErrorEvent_h/docu.output.md`



## PythonCrashedEvent

**Role:** `PythonCrashedEvent` is a lightweight, immutable event type that signals an unrecoverable failure in the embedded Python subsystem. It carries a human-readable diagnostic message describing the nature of the crash and propagates through the engine's event bus so that listeners (logging systems, UI layers, workflow supervisors) can react appropriately. It belongs to `EventCategoryEngine` and uses the event type token `PythonCrashed`, which the macro infrastructure uses for type identification and dispatch.

**Public API:**

- `PythonCrashedEvent(std::string message)` — Constructor. Takes ownership of `message` via `std::move`. Stores the crash description for later retrieval. No side effects beyond object initialisation; does not interact with the event bus itself.
- `GetMessage() const → const std::string&` — Returns a const reference to the stored crash description. Valid for the lifetime of the event object; callers must not store the reference beyond that.
- `GetStaticType() → EventType` (injected by `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE(PythonCrashed)`) — Returns the compile-time `EventType::PythonCrashed` enum value used by the dispatcher for type matching.
- `GetEventType() const → EventType` (injected by `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`) — Instance-level type query; returns `EventType::PythonCrashed`.
- `GetName() const → const char*` (injected by `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE`) — Returns the string `"PythonCrashed"`, typically used for logging.
- `GetCategoryFlags() const → int` (injected by `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY(EventCategoryEngine)`) — Returns the bitmask for `EventCategoryEngine`, enabling category-based filtering in the event dispatcher.

**Collaborators:**

- `event/event.h` — Provides the `Event` base class and the `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` / `EVENT_CLASS_CATEGORY` macros. The base class defines the interface expected by the event bus dispatcher, including `Handled`, `GetEventType`, and `GetCategoryFlags`.
- Embedded Python subsystem — The component responsible for constructing and firing this event when Python execution fails fatally. The exact producer class is not visible in this file.
- Event bus / dispatcher — The engine component that receives and routes events; it matches against `EventType::PythonCrashed` and the `EventCategoryEngine` bitmask to deliver the event to registered listeners.

**Threading / lifetime:**

- `PythonCrashedEvent` objects are value-type events with no shared state or heap-allocated collaborators beyond the internal `std::string`. They are typically stack-allocated at the crash site and passed by reference into the dispatch call.
- The object must remain alive for the full duration of the synchronous dispatch chain. If the event bus dispatches on the same thread that constructed the event (the common j9t pattern for engine-category events), this is naturally satisfied.
- No locking is performed by this class. Thread safety for concurrent dispatch is the responsibility of the event bus.

**Notes:**

- The `EVENT_CLASS_TYPE` macro registers `PythonCrashed` as a distinct enumerator in `EventType`; that enumerator must exist in the enum defined in `event/event.h` or the project will fail to compile.
- `EventCategoryEngine` categorisation means this event will pass category filters intended for engine-level events but will not match UI or application category filters.
- The event carries no structured data beyond the message string — no exception object, no Python traceback object, no error code. Callers that need richer diagnostics must embed that information in the message string before construction.
- `Handled` (inherited from `Event`) defaults to `false`. A listener that handles the crash notification should set it to prevent redundant downstream handling, but nothing in this class enforces that.

### 127_doc_engine_json_configParser_h

<a id="127-doc-engine-json-configparser-h"></a>

*Source doc:* `../../../queue/jarvisCppDocu/127_doc_engine_json_configParser_h/docu.output.md`



## ConfigParser

**Role:**  
The `AIAssistant::ConfigParser` class is responsible for reading, parsing, and validating the system-wide configuration for the j9t AI workflow engine. It handles the loading of a JSON configuration file (typically `config.json`), extracts both global engine settings and detailed definitions of AI provider interfaces (including their rate limits, timeouts, and model-specific parameters), and populates an `EngineConfig` structure. This configuration governs job queuing, request budgeting, concurrency limits, file paths, Python embedding, API credentials, and network/security options for all workflow engine operations.

**Public API:**

- `ConfigParser(std::string const&)` — Constructs a ConfigParser bound to a configuration file specified by a full path string. Does not load or parse until `Parse()` is called.
- `~ConfigParser()` — Destructor. No explicit resource management.
- `State GetState() const` — Returns the last parsing state/result (`Undefined`, `ConfigOk`, `ParseFailure`, `FileNotFound`, `FileFormatFailure`).
- `State Parse(EngineConfig&)` — Loads the config file, parses its JSON, fills in the passed-in `EngineConfig&` with settings/interfaces, and sets internal state. Input must be a by-reference `EngineConfig` (reset on entry). Returns the parse state. Side effects: logs diagnostics, may throw/halt if JSON is misformed.
- `bool ConfigParsed() const` — Returns true iff the last parse succeeded and state is `ConfigOk`.

**EngineConfig inner API (part of the config structure, not the parser itself):**
- `static std::string GenerateInterfaceName(std::string const& url, std::string const& model, std::string const& apiType)` — Generates a unique interface name from a URL domain, model, and API type.
- `static uint64_t ResolveMaxContextTokensFromModel(std::string const& modelName)` — Determines the default context token limit for an AI model, using an internal lookup/fallback table.
- `bool IsValid() const` — Returns whether this `EngineConfig` is valid (determined by parsing outcome).

**Collaborators:**

- Depends on `simdjson` for high-performance JSON parsing.
- Uses `EngineCore::FileExists` and `EngineCore::IsDirectory` (presumably from `engine.h`) to validate file presence.
- Relies on logging macros like `LOG_CORE_ERROR`, `LOG_CORE_INFO`, `LOG_CORE_WARN`, and assertions such as `CORE_ASSERT` and `CORE_HARD_STOP` for diagnostics and hard-failures.
- Works with `"auxiliary/file.h"` for file path and possibly file IO utilities.
- The resulting configuration is consumed by the main engine (via the populated `EngineConfig`), which governs job dispatch, provider selection, and request handling logic.
- Collaborates with other engine components (not shown here) that use AI interface metadata, queuing folders, credentials, and concurrency settings.

**Threading / lifetime:**

- `ConfigParser` objects are constructed, parsed, and then discarded or reused as needed—their lifetime is controlled by callers (typically setup/init code).
- No explicit thread safety or locking is implemented; not thread-safe for concurrent access.
- Methods assume single-threaded use. The filled `EngineConfig` should not be mutated during engine operation except at startup/reload.
- No ownership of file or external resources is retained after parsing (no open handles, etc).

**Notes:**

- Parsing is strict: missing required fields (like queue folder or at least one interface URL) will cause parsing to fail (`FileFormatFailure`).
- The parser detects duplicate/missing fields and logs all recognized and unrecognized JSON keys for troubleshooting.
- The `EngineConfig` and its nested structs provide default values for most settings, but optional configuration fields in JSON may override them.
- The parser automatically estimates `max_context_tokens` for interfaces when not set in config, using a model-name substring matching against a hardcoded table of popular providers/models.
- Interface names are auto-generated from domain/model/type if absent, ensuring uniqueness.
- Each API interface can specify its own rate limits, retry strategy, size budget, and output tokens for granular control per provider.
- The parser is case- and underscore-sensitive and expects exact JSON field names as coded.
- Any unknown fields in the config are logged but ignored.
- Internal state (`m_State`) always reflects the result of the last parse attempt, enabling repeated parse/reload cycles if needed.
- Only reads the config file on `Parse()`; does not watch for file changes or support runtime hot-reloading (this must be handled elsewhere).
- Configuration for secrets (`keys.json.enc`, `mcp_keys.json.enc`) is loaded by setting file paths—not the secrets themselves—here.
- Will abort (`CORE_HARD_STOP`) on unrecognized API type strings in interface definitions.
- The existence of Python engine counts and workflow settings signals tight integration with multi-language plugin support.
- Not all config fields are mandatory; logging extensively assists with partial/malformed configs.
- Defaults (such as API request budgets, output token counts, and fallback context window) are chosen conservatively to minimize provider-side errors or dropped requests.

This class provides all the configuration management and validation required for robust, multi-provider AI workflow orchestration in j9t, abstracting JSON parsing details and ensuring the engine operates with complete, invariant-respecting config data.
